notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup (referral via community Slack). Trial began 2026-02-01 (first API key issued). 

Summary: small engineering shop building an embeddable developer helper inside their web IDE. Primary interest was low-friction Hosted API for chat + embeddings. Team picked a single dev key and ran a handful of smoke tests; did not ramp beyond simple echo/prompt flows. Usage dropped to near-zero after first week. Customer has been evaluating OpenAI/Anthropic + Cohere; mentioned competitor promotional credits as a reason to pause. 

Quote from CTO (2026-02-10): 'Liked the latency and cost estimates, but our CFO is pushing for the $10k credits OpenAI offered — need to justify switching.' 

Security: asked about SSO (SAML), audit logs, and retention controls. We provided SOC2 summary and SAML doc (drive links above) but they want explicit retention options for embeddings (can we TTL vectors?). 

POC notes / timeline: 
- 2026-02-01: self-serve signup, AE assigned automatically, welcome email sent (Maya). 
- 2026-02-03: Maya 15m intro call — scope: in-IDE dev assistant, 50–200 concurrent users long-term, initial test users 2–3 devs. Asked about cost per 1k tokens and latency SLOs. 
- 2026-02-04: dev team spun up single API key and ran simple prompts + embeddings indexing (~1200 tokens/day first 3 days). 
- 2026-02-11: automated usage alert triggered (low usage). Maya followed up by email; dev said they are 'paused' pending procurement decision and competitor credits. 
- 2026-02-18: SE session (Ethan) ran 30m troubleshooting session to show batching and caching to reduce token spend; provided a sample config and quick benchmark (p95 latency ~120ms on 4k context). 
- 2026-02-22: provided pricing comparison and a tailored 2-week credits offer (emailed). 
- 2026-03-05: customer replied: likely to try competitor credits first; will circle back if results poor. 

Current health: AT-RISK. Trial effectively stalled — single key, very low token consumption, signal of churn due to competitor crediting. No security red flags but unanswered question around embeddings TTL + retention is slowing procurement. 

Recommendation / Next steps: 
- Short-term (this week): Offer a targeted re-engagement package: 1 month $500 credits + 30-min workshop focused on prompt engineering + batching to demonstrate cost reduction. Schedule proposed: 2026-03-17. 
- Medium-term: Provide a one-page competitive note (benchmarks + cost per effective response with batching) and a clear doc on embeddings retention/TTL options and how to configure via Hosted API. 
- Escalation: If they indicate competitor is final, ask for a short feedback call and a churn-back offer (trial top-up + implementation support). 

Streaks / misc: internal note that marketing had a small promo overlap week of 2026-02-09; competitor activity likely influenced decision. Consider targeted win-back drip if they do not respond after re-engage date.
